links_touching_record.rationale: Software requirement allocated from functional safety requirement

FB2-SW-IMP-000003 realises the actuation and feedback-confirmation clauses of the reference project's FB2-SW-SWR-000003, with the sequencing realised one layer above in BMS_Trigger, and declares the design's cycle counter a not_in_source proposal. The requirement's 5 ms emergency-open clause is not established by this link and the configured waits the source applies are longer.

FB2-SW-SWR-000003 is allocated to the reference project's FB2-SW-DSN-000003 as the software requirement whose implementation that design details. The design additionally claims sequencing and cycle counting the requirement does not state and the source does not realise; that difference is recorded on the implementation record rather than hidden by this link.
Architectural element AR-004 of the technical safety concept is realised by FB2-SW-SWR-000003. The element's role and the record's statement were read against each other.

FB2-SW-SWR-000003 is the lower-level requirement allocated to the system requirement FB2-SYS-SYR-000003. The two statements and acceptance criteria were read against each other before the link was made, so the system requirement is covered indirectly through its allocation rather than directly by a measure of its own.

FB2-SW-SWR-000003 is the lower-level requirement allocated to the system requirement FB2-SYS-SYR-000004. The two statements and acceptance criteria were read against each other before the link was made, so the system requirement is covered indirectly through its allocation rather than directly by a measure of its own.

FB2-SW-SWR-000003 is the lower-level requirement allocated to the system requirement FB2-SYS-SYR-000008. The two statements and acceptance criteria were read against each other before the link was made, so the system requirement is covered indirectly through its allocation rather than directly by a measure of its own.

The requirement's three acceptance criteria are 5 ms fault-response latency, 100% auxiliary feedback readback and 100% valid state transitions. The specification records that the contactor driver's only test does not build, so none of the three has any result, and the plan's PC-008 requires a measured clock for the latency criterion.

integrity.anchor_registry_note: The corpus provenance gate verifies each anchor against the file that anchor names and stores no registry-level digest of its own. This digest is recorded so a signature also pins which anchor set was in force.
integrity.verbatim_block_note: The block in section 3 is the file's decoded text with any single trailing newline removed, which is what the markdown fences require. `record_sha256` above is over the raw file bytes and is the digest a signature refers to; this one is over the text as embedded, so a verifier can compare either.

questions_for_human.question: As the sw_engineer for this software record, do you agree that "The contactor driver shall execute state machine (OPEN -> PRECHARGE -> CLOSE -> HOLD) and open contactors within 5 ms of FAULT state request from SOA/DIAG." is a correct and complete statement of software requirements, architecture, detailed design, implementation mapping, unit verification?
questions_for_human.why_this_needs_a_human: Correctness of engineering content is not derivable from the repository. The corpus can prove the record is well-formed and internally consistent; it cannot prove the engineering is right.

questions_for_human.question: Are the acceptance criteria complete and decidable - could a verifier say with certainty whether this requirement is met?
questions_for_human.what_in_this_packet_bears_on_it: acceptance_criteria and verification_approach in the record.
questions_for_human.why_this_needs_a_human: An undecidable requirement cannot be verified, and the corpus cannot tell an undecidable requirement from a merely terse one.

shape_note: Deliberately not shaped like a corpus record: no top-level id, profile, artifact_type or source_refs, so that generating packets cannot change any coverage number. See the module docstring of make_review_packets.py.

signature_block._recording: Transcribe a completed signature into the record as human_approval_status plus a revision_history entry naming the reviewer, and archive the signed packet outside docs/artifacts/reviews/packets/.
signature_block._rule: Empty by construction. No automated process may fill this. Filling it in is the only thing that changes human_approval_status on the record, and the corpus rule `human_approval_rejected` fails validation on any record whose human_approval_status is not pending, so no tool can manufacture the state.

signature_policy: The signature block below is empty by construction. This tool has no code path that writes a decision, an approval, a signature or an execution verdict. Filling it is a human action.
